goal: Produce six independent attempts at the smallest useful ResonantOS meeting ontology, using two repetitions of three distinct perspectives, then summarize their convergences, divergences, and smallest defensible common core.
context: The existing ResonantOS meeting documents contain a broad candidate vocabulary that has not been validated. The user wants fewer concepts, tentative definitions only for small bounded things, and independent attempts rather than premature consensus. Treat all existing meeting-model vocabulary as candidate evidence, not as a required starting schema.

agents.initial_prompt: Work independently from the participant/newcomer perspective. Read only research/resonantos-meetings/research-initial-definitions.md, research-plan.md, ontology-view.md, system-view.md, engineer-view.md, and paired-views-report.md. Do not read minimal-ontology-exploration or any other agent output. Ask: what is the smallest ontology a participant or newcomer needs to understand what a meeting is and how to relate to it? Use no minimum and at most five concepts. For every concept give a one-sentence tentative definition, why it is irreducible, and the exact loss caused by removing it. Distinguish concepts from attributes, values, relations, labels, and mechanics. Include only necessary typed relations. End with small optional proposals and deliberate omissions. Existing vocabulary is candidate evidence, not required structure. Make no novelty claim and use no web sources. Write only research/resonantos-meetings/minimal-ontology-exploration/attempts/a-participant.md, then return a concise handoff.
